summary: Famicom Disk System golf releases from Nintendo and HAL, with Disk Fax contest prize disks treated as secondary exclusive-course content.

entries.title: Family Computer Golf: Japan Course
entries.definitive_edition: Original Family Computer Disk System blue disk, plus gold-disk prize courses as secondary content

emulation.emulator: Mesen or ares with Famicom Disk System support
emulation.notes: Use accurate FDS emulation with the BIOS and legal disk dumps; verify save/disk-write behavior because the original used Disk Fax score data. Preserve 4:3 and avoid enhancement filters for archival capture.

primary.version: Original blue-disk Golf: Japan Course release
primary.why: Golf: Japan Course is a February 21, 1987 NES/Famicom Disk System release developed by HAL Laboratory and published by Nintendo, with Famicom Disk System media. There is no later platform or remaster, so the highest-fidelity main route is a clean dump of the original blue disk in accurate FDS emulation. The gold prize disks add exclusive harder courses, but they replace the course content rather than serving as the normal main version.
primary.how_to_play: Use a legally dumped original Family Computer Golf: Japan Course blue disk in an accurate Famicom Disk System emulator such as Mesen or ares. Preserve 4:3, original timing, and disk-write/save behavior; after the main retail 18-hole route, play the Professional Course and Champions' Course prize disks only as secondary exclusive-course mop-ups if verified copies/dumps are available.

secondary.platform: Family Computer Disk System - Golf: Japan Course (Professional Course)
secondary.exclusive_content: Gold-disk prize version with a harder alternate 18-hole course, given to tournament runners-up.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the Professional Course holes as a secondary run after completing or sampling the retail Japan Course.
secondary.why: Professional Course was a special Golf: Japan Course release on FDS with more difficult holes, one of the gold-disk tournament prizes for the Family Computer Disk System.

secondary.platform: Family Computer Disk System - Golf: Japan Course (Champions' Course)
secondary.exclusive_content: Very rare gold-disk prize version for top tournament winners with a different, harder course layout; public preservation appears incomplete.
secondary.what_to_play: Treat as an archive target and play only if a verified dump or physical capture becomes available; otherwise document its missing/inaccessible status.
secondary.why: Champions' Course was a separate tournament prize for 100 winners, and the game has not been dumped, so it is real exclusive content but not reliably playable today.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced remaster, port, or official modern reissue was found. The Disk Fax tournament/service features are defunct, and Champions' Course is documented as not publicly dumped, so full archival completeness may require rare physical access.

primary.version: Original blue-disk Golf: U.S. Course release
primary.why: Golf: US Course, also known as Family Computer Golf: U.S. Course, is a June 14, 1987 NES/Famicom Disk System release by HAL Laboratory and Nintendo, and is the companion to Japan Course with Disk Fax compatibility. No later platform or remaster exists, so accurate FDS emulation of the retail blue disk is the primary route; the gold Golf: Special Course prize disk is secondary because it adds a harder special course rather than replacing the normal U.S. Course.
primary.how_to_play: Use a legally dumped Golf: U.S. Course blue disk in Mesen or ares with Famicom Disk System support. Preserve 4:3 and original timing; after the retail U.S. Course route, play Golf: Special Course only as a secondary exclusive-course run if a verified copy/dump is available.

secondary.platform: Family Computer Disk System - Golf: Special Course
secondary.exclusive_content: Gold-disk prize version of Golf: U.S. Course with a harder Special Course and a hidden female character unlock route.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the Special Course after the retail U.S. Course; optionally document the hidden character condition if using a verified dump/copy.
secondary.why: Golf: Special Course was a special Golf: U.S. Course release distributed as a prize, with a harder course and hidden character details.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced remaster, port, or official modern reissue was found. Disk Fax contest functionality is defunct, and the Special Course gold disk was a limited prize item rather than a normal retail release.
